title: Can every fraction greater than one be written as a mixed number?
description: Eight fourths and nine fourths are each split into wholes and leftover parts. The board shows that eight fourths leaves nothing over, so it is only a whole number, while nine fourths leaves a fraction.
teaching_notes: One idea: a mixed number needs a fraction part that is more than zero. Watch for students who think every fraction greater than one must have a fraction left over.

source: Figure it Out Q2 (section 7.5, second block)
video_script.why: A learner tests when a fraction greater than one has no fraction left after the wholes are taken out.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question, with eight fourths and nine fourths as the test fractions
video_script.anchor: a row of eight fourth bars and a row of nine fourth bars
video_script.payoff_line: No, not every fraction greater than one can be written as a mixed number

final_answer.value: No. 8/4 = 2 has nothing left over, so it is a whole number and not a mixed number.
final_answer.spoken: no, eight fourths is the whole number two, with nothing left over

video_script.fraction_reading: four fourths, eight fourths, nine fourths, one fourth
maths_rules: a mixed number is a whole number plus a fraction that is more than 0 and less than 1
video_script.design: A row of eight fourth bars joins into two whole bars with nothing left. A row of nine fourth bars joins into two whole bars with one fourth left.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it is about fractions.
<bookmark mark='def'/>A whole number together with a fraction less than one is called a mixed number.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can every fraction greater than one be written as a mixed number?

narration: <bookmark mark='need'/>A mixed number needs a whole part. It also needs a fraction part more than zero.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, we test two fractions, eight fourths and nine fourths.

beats.on_screen: To find: does each one leave a fraction after the wholes are taken out
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find if each one leaves a fraction after the wholes are taken out.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 8/4 = 4/4 + 4/4, which is 2 groups of 4 fourths

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, we use the same way as the examples in your book. Eight fourths is four fourths and four fourths.
<bookmark mark='two'/>These are two groups of four fourths, so there are two wholes.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: nothing is left over, so 8/4 is the whole number 2

marks.none: no fourth bar is left after the two whole bars
marks.whole: eight fourths is written as the whole number two, with no fraction part

narration: <bookmark mark='none'/>Step two, nothing is left over after the two wholes.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>Eight fourths has no fraction part, so it is the whole number two.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 9/4 = 8/4 + 1/4, so 2 wholes and 1/4 is left over

marks.split: nine fourths is split into eight fourths and one fourth
marks.left: one fourth bar stays alone after the two whole bars

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step three, nine fourths is eight fourths and one fourth.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Two wholes come out and one fourth is left, so nine fourths is a mixed number.

marks.one: two groups of four fourths are put back together as eight fourths
marks.two: two groups of four fourths and one fourth are put back together as nine fourths

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>To check, put the pieces back together. Two groups of four fourths make eight fourths, with nothing added.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two groups of four fourths and one fourth make nine fourths, so a fraction is left.

beats.on_screen: Answer: No. 8/4 = 2 has nothing left over, so it is a whole number and not a mixed number.

marks.eight: eight fourths is shown as the whole number two
marks.nine: nine fourths is shown as two wholes and one fourth

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>No, not every fraction greater than one can be written as a mixed number.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Eight fourths is the whole number two, with nothing left over.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Nine fourths is a mixed number, because one fourth is left.
